The spring 2024 survey covered more than 95,000 respondents at 20 research-intensive public universities; it does not establish subsequent employer difficulty.

evidence_items.explanation: The February–March 2026 survey of 185 employers reports broadly positive graduate preparedness and substantial alignment with hiring needs, alongside weaknesses in communication, professionalism, and critical thinking. This weighs against an already widespread educational failure, but measures neither recruitment difficulty caused by cheating nor changes in graduate learning attributable to GenAI.

unresolved_gaps: No located evidence links college GenAI cheating, measured learning deficiencies, and subsequent employer recruitment difficulty in the same population.
Employer preparedness ratings do not establish whether suitable graduates have become harder to find.
The available evidence does not separate the proposed educational mechanism from other causes of hiring or skill gaps.
The forecast provides no deadline at which continued absence of the predicted outcome would constitute failure.
